title: Zelensky Accuses Pentagon of Delaying Patriot Missile Shipments as U.S.-Ukraine Tensions Escalate
snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed Washington is stalling European transfers of Patriot interceptors as diplomatic friction between Kyiv and the Trump administration deepens.
content:
WASHINGTON — Friction between Kyiv and Washington reached a new flashpoint Tuesday as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused the U.S. Department of Defense of sitting on crucial approvals needed to deliver Patriot air defense systems to his war-torn nation.

Addressing U.S. lawmakers, Zelensky stated that multiple European allies are ready to supply Ukraine with Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles, but the transfers are stuck waiting on a signature from U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Stalled Defenses Amid Russian Strikes

The delay comes at a perilous moment for Ukraine, as relentless Russian strikes continue targeting energy grid infrastructure, leaving hundreds of thousands of citizens without electricity ahead of the winter months. Zelensky urged Washington to expedite the missile transfers and demanded the full restoration of the Starshield satellite system, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications.

Despite concerns over restricted service on Starshield, President Donald Trump has denied ordering any throttling of the U.S.-controlled satellite network, while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio maintained that intelligence sharing with Kyiv remains intact.

Diplomatic Rift with the Trump Administration

The dispute over military hardware highlights a widening rift between Zelensky and the White House. Relations have frayed further following President Trump's partial lifting of Russian sanctions to secure a diesel supply deal, alongside public criticism targeting Zelensky's strategy of striking Russian oil refineries.

Trump recently suggested that "somebody else" should take over peace negotiations for Kyiv and floated potential high-level talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing next month—a proposal Ukrainian officials warn could sideline their sovereignty and encourage further aggression from Moscow.

High-Stakes Negotiations in Norway

In an effort to reset diplomatic channels, Zelensky is participating in talks in Oslo hosted by Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb. U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are joining the summit to push for a constructive path forward, with reports indicating Witkoff may subsequently travel to Moscow to meet directly with Kremlin leaders.
